newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta share index maintains losses.
newsitem.headline: Malta share index maintains losses.

text.p: The Malta share index shed a further 7.16 points on Wednesday to close at 967.02.
The index lost 11.44 points in the previous once weekly session, with stockbrokers reporting relatively heavy selling of equities, possibly in anticipation of new government debt issues.
Finance Minister Lino Spiteri in his budget speech on Monday confirmed that the new Labour government would have to continue borrowing to finance its deficit.
Turnover this Wednesday reached just over 1,9 million Maltese pounds ($5.4 million) up from 317,100 pounds in the previous week. Trading was spread over 103 deals, of which only 33 were in equities.
Equities trading amounted to 35,855 pounds, with 27,245 shares changing hands.
Of these, 11,980 were Bank of Valletta shares transacted in 12 deals at an average price of 119 cents, a loss of three cents.
There were 16 deals in Mid-Med Bank with 13,070 shares selling for an average 146.3 cents, down one cent.
Lombard Bank Malta also traded, with 1,500 shares selling for an average 139 cents, down one cent. Farsons ordinary shares held their price, with 695 shares selling for an average 50 cents each.

Trading was up in government bonds, reaching 1.95 million pounds from the previous week's 136,500 pounds. Business was dominated by large deals in the 6.3 percent MGS 1999 (IV) and the 6.75 percent MGS 1997 issues.
